\section{Introduction}
When a hot body exchanges heat with a colder body, their temperatures approach one another. Energy conservation constrains the common final state, whereas the contact law determines how quickly it is approached. A pair of finite bodies makes this distinction explicit because both temperatures evolve.

This synthetic example connects the transient temperatures, equilibrium state, and entropy balance for two internally equilibrated reservoirs with fixed heat capacities and a linear contact law. Conservation determines a weighted mean temperature. The temperature difference then obeys a closed decay equation, from which positivity and the sign of entropy production follow. The accompanying synthetic notes specify the assumptions and algebra; they provide no external prior-work evidence. No new transport law or experimental measurement is claimed.

The result concerns the exact solution of stipulated equations. Establishing that those equations describe a particular apparatus would require evidence beyond this example.
